questions.question: Which heading tag denotes the highest level of structural importance in HTML?
questions.explanation: <h1> represents the top-level heading in the document hierarchy.

questions.question: What is the primary semantic meaning of the <hr> tag in HTML5?
options: A thematic break or transition between topics
A hard reboot of the DOM parser
questions.hint: It represents a thematic shift in the content.
questions.explanation: In HTML5, <hr> semantically represents a thematic break between paragraphs or sections.

questions.question: Why is it discouraged to skip heading levels (e.g., jumping from <h1> directly to <h3>)?
options: It causes browsers to crash on mobile devices
It creates confusion for screen reader users and impairs accessibility
It invalidates the SSL security certificate
It prevents CSS styles from being applied
questions.hint: Think about assistive technology navigating the document outline.
questions.explanation: Skipping heading levels confuses users of assistive technologies like screen readers who use headings to navigate the page.

questions.question: Which tag is best suited for breaking an address onto multiple lines inside a paragraph?
questions.hint: A void tag that creates a single line break.
questions.explanation: produces a line break within text where line divisions are part of the content.

questions.question: How many <h1> tags are recommended per page for SEO and accessibility best practices?
options: Unlimited as long as they are bold
questions.explanation: Having a single <h1> element per page provides a clear, unambiguous title for users, screen readers, and search engines.
